deep.reconstruction:
Page headed '⊗ dans Cat' (tensor products in Cat). The page sets up a 2-categorical dictionary between small k-linear categories and their categories of additive presheaves. This dictionary is presumably meant as preparation for a tensor product of cocomplete k-linear categories, of the form P^& ⊗ Q^& := (P ⊗_k Q)^&, inside the 'Abelianization' project.

(1) Definition. Let P be a small k-additive category. Put P^& := Hom_Z(P°, Ab), the additive presheaves on P. This is equivalent to Hom_k(P°, Mod_k), because any additive functor out of a k-linear category inherits a canonical k-module structure on its values. So P^& depends only on the underlying additive category, as Grothendieck notes.

(2) Yoneda and Karoubi envelope. The Yoneda embedding P → P^& is additive and fully faithful. It extends to Kar P → P^&, which identifies the Karoubi (idempotent/Cauchy) completion with UlProj(P^&). UlProj is presumably the 'ultra-projective' objects, i.e. small (compact) projectives. As a consequence (Kar P)^& ≃ P^&: Morita invariance under Cauchy completion.

(3) Recognition theorem. A k-additive category 𝒫 is k-equivalent to some P^& if and only if:
(a) 𝒫 is a 'topos abélien', i.e. a Grothendieck abelian category: abelian, with exact filtered colimits, and a small generating subcategory;
(b) 𝒫 has enough projectives.
One may then take P = UlProj(𝒫). This is the Gabriel–Freyd–Mitchell characterization of module categories over 'rings with several objects'.

(4) 2-categorical packaging. There is a 2-functor Add_k → Topab_k, called 2-essentially surjective. It factors through Kar: Add_k → AddKar_k, and the second factor AddKar_k → Topab_k is called '3-fid.' (presumably 2-fully faithful: equivalences on Hom-categories).
- Morphisms of k-abelian topoi are defined by analogy with essential geometric morphisms of topoi. They are colimit-preserving f_!: 𝒫 → 𝒬 whose right adjoint f^* also preserves colimits, i.e. has a further right adjoint f_*.
- Such an f^* is exact and cocontinuous, so f_! preserves small projectives. Hence these morphisms correspond to k-functors Kar P → Kar Q, which explains the full faithfulness on AddKar_k.

(5) Free cocompletion. Every L in P^& is the canonical colimit L ≃ lim→_{P/L} a (density of Yoneda). Hence restriction gives Hom_{k!}(P^&, M) ≃ Hom_k(P, M) for any k-additive cocomplete M; Hom_{k!} denotes colimit-preserving functors. Dually, Hom_k^!(P^{&°}, M) ≃ Hom_k(P°, M) for complete M, with limit-preserving functors. Setting Q = P° gives Hom^!(Q^{&°}, M) ≃ Hom_k(P, M).

These universal properties are exactly what is needed to define and characterize a tensor product of such 'abelian topoi'.

Dating: the verso/next sheet is a line-printer separator dated 16 Sep 82, consistent with the archive's 'à partir de 1982' (just before Pursuing Stacks).
errors: Condition (b) 'assez de projectifs' is too weak as stated. The correct criterion (Freyd/Mitchell/Gabriel) needs a generating family of SMALL projectives: projectives P with Hom(P,-) commuting with direct sums or filtered colimits. The parenthetical 'P = UlProj(𝒫)' shows Grothendieck intended these compact projectives, so (b) should read 'assez d'ultra-projectifs'.

Accordingly, Add_k → Topab_k is 2-essentially surjective only onto the full sub-2-category of Grothendieck abelian categories generated by small projectives, not onto all 'topos abéliens' in the sense of (a).

'3-fid.' is non-standard; the correct statement is that AddKar_k → Topab_k is fully faithful at the level of Hom-categories (with morphisms f_! having a cocontinuous right adjoint). Add_k → Topab_k itself is not, because Kar is not an equivalence.

ideas.what: P^& = additive presheaves; independence from the k-structure; Yoneda embedding
ideas.modern_name: additive/k-linear presheaf category (free cocompletion of a k-linear category)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mitchell ('Rings with several objects', 1972), Freyd; enriched version Kelly (1982)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related discussions in Pursuing Stacks (1983) on linear categories and abelianization; unsure

ideas.what: Kar P ≃ small projectives of P^&, and (Kar P)^& ≃ P^&
ideas.where_published: Karoubi envelopes appear in Grothendieck's motives circle (Demazure/Manin) but not in this form

ideas.what: Characterization of P^& as Grothendieck abelian categories with enough (small) projectives
Calling Grothendieck abelian categories 'topos abéliens', with morphisms modelled on essential geometric morphisms (f_!, f^*, f_*)
ideas.modern_name: linear analogue of essential geometric morphisms; locally presentable k-linear categories with left adjoints having cocontinuous right adjoints
ideas.usually_credited_to: analogy implicit in SGA4 module categories; enriched setting Street, Kelly

ideas.what: Universal property Hom_!(P^&, M) ≃ Hom(P, M) and its dual with limits, leading to a tensor product in Cat
ideas.modern_name: free cocompletion universal property; Kelly tensor product of cocomplete linear categories (P⊗Q)^&
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly (Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory, 1982); later Deligne (1990) for abelian tensor products

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames additive presheaf categories as 'abelian topoi', with morphisms defined like essential geometric morphisms (f_! ⊣ f^* ⊣ f_*), in preparation for a tensor product in Cat, around Sept 1982. This documents his independent use of the Cauchy-completion/Morita 2-categorical viewpoint shortly before Pursuing Stacks. It is historically interesting but mathematically standard (Freyd, Mitchell, Kelly, Street).

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Small historical data point on the genesis of Grothendieck's linear/abelianization ideas (Pursuing Stacks, derivators). No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Content is classical Morita/Cauchy-completion and free-cocompletion theory, already known by 1982 (Freyd, Mitchell, Kelly, Street). The only notable features are the 'topos abélien' terminology, the geometric-morphism-style definition of morphisms, and the dating via the printer sheet (Sept 1982).
transcription_corrections: 'Ab_k' is written as Ab with subscript k; in the Hom_{k!} line the target is a script M with subscript k (𝓜_k), not plain 'M_k'.
'Posons' is crossed out and replaced by 'et alors'. The parenthesis reads '(il suffit de prendre P = UlProj(𝒫))'. 'UlProj' probably abbreviates small or 'ultra' projectives.
In the 2-functor diagram the label reads '3-fid.' beside the arrow AddKar_k → Topab_k; the top arrow is labelled '2-ess. surj' (an earlier abbreviation is crossed out).
The crossed-out line is Hom_{Z!}(P^&, Ab) ≈ Hom_Z(P, Ab).
The next page is a line-printer separator dated 16 SEP 82, which dates the reuse of paper (terminus post quem).
